title: Field extension in dimension zero
statement:
Let $k\subset k'$ be algebraically closed fields, let $C$ be a separated
finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension at most zero, and let $F$ be a torsion
etale sheaf on $C$, so that $(C,F)$ is a curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]. The pullback map
$\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,F):H^q(C_{\Et},F)\to H^q((C_{k'})_{\Et},\pi^{-1}F)$ along the projection $\pi:C_{k'}=C\times_kk'\to C$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-pullback], i.e. the map $\pi^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], is an isomorphism for every $q\geq0$.

proof.text: For q=0, use bijectivity of the canonical global-sections pullback. Compose Sheaf.H.equiv₀ with ΓNatIsoSheafSections to identify H^0 with Γ on both schemes. cohomologyMap_zero_eq_globalSectionsUpperStarMap identifies the specified cohomology map with the conjugate of the sections map, hence makes it bijective.

For q>0 choose the algebraic-closure points C.algClosurePoint. zero_dimensional_etale_cohomology gives subsingleton derived cohomology; evaluate the natural Ext/derived isomorphism on F and use its injectivity to deduce subsingleton Sheaf.H.

Write the bottom morphism as Spec.map a and give k′ the algebra structure induced by a. zeroDimensional_baseChange_points gives the dimension bound on the canonical pullback. Transfer it to C′ using h.isoPullback and invariance of topological Krull dimension under a homeomorphism. Separatedness, local finite type and quasi-compactness of f′ follow by stability under base change.

Apply the positive-degree vanishing argument to both the original abelian sheaf and its inverse image on C′. A map between two zero abelian groups is injective by Subsingleton.elim and surjective using the zero preimage. The degree-zero and positive-degree cases exhaust all natural numbers.
